items.title: 61520_Teddy Edwards oral history interview
items.q: The personnel was Earl (?) on piano, Bob Kesterson, bass, and Roy Porter, drums.

ctx.x: But anyway, before that... Howard had lots of records, Classical records or Jazz records, all the latest things, you know. So a lot of people used to hang there and listen to the sides all the time. It was like a music house. The Treniers were living right across the walkway in their place, the Trenier Twins and all their gang. Moses Brown became one of my real great friends later on in life, and Gene Gilbo(?), the piano player and orchestrator who was with them.

But anyway, we all used to hang around through there. And so, Howard formed this band to go into the Finale Club on First and San Pedro. The personnel was Earl (?) on piano, Bob Kesterson, bass, and Roy Porter, drums. And we had Gene Montgomery on tenor, Sonny Criss on alto, Charlie Parker on the other alto, and I'm on the tenor. That was the saxophone section. It was too bad this band wasn't recorded. It was during the recording ban. Do you remember the recording ban, when they struck, the American Federation of…
We had a vocalist named Bill Jones. Now, do you remember Bill Jones?
